name: Missinglettr
tagline: Turns blog content into scheduled social campaigns and curated posts

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

verdictSummary: The visible content repurposing loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Missinglettr earns its keep through platform APIs, distribution, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a personal content repurposing planner that stores drafts, previews platform variants, and exports a posting queue without pretending to bypass platform APIs.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: official platform OAuth credentials where available
whatYouLose: protection from API and policy changes
direct publishing reliability as platform APIs change
whyPeopleStillPay: Missinglettr: Social tools survive because networks change APIs, permissions, formats, and anti-spam rules constantly.
ongoingBurden: Maintain OAuth, token refresh, media constraints, rate limits, scheduling, webhooks, retries, and platform policy compliance.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Open-source social scheduling and publishing platform.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Mixpost Lite
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Evergreen queues are present; turning one article into a finished campaign is still manual.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Postiz
rejectedAlternatives.desc: RSS auto-posting and repeats exist, but not the blog-to-campaign generator or curated-content loop.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Missinglettr is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Missinglettr, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + BullMQ.
Primary job: Build a personal content repurposing planner that stores drafts, previews platform variants, and exports a posting queue without pretending to bypass platform APIs.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: analytics history and attribution; team approvals and asset workflows; protection from API and policy changes.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
